reader.reads: Read the two English verses on p. 29 of the 1888 Boston Nonsense Books beside register A:E145 and A:R134.

thesis.ru: Старушка из Чертси сделала замечательный реверанс. Она кружилась до самого ухода под землю, чем огорчила всех жителей Чертси.
thesis.en: The Old Lady of Chertsey made a remarkable curtsey. She twirled round and round until she sank underground, distressing all the people of Chertsey.

conceptions.note: The register describes a technique and changes in expectations; this conception follows the particular verse and does not attribute that analysis to the verse as a philosophical thesis.

thesis.ru: Подбородок молодой леди походил на острие булавки; она велела его заострить, купила арфу и сыграла на ней несколько мелодий подбородком.
thesis.en: The Young Lady’s chin resembled the point of a pin; she had it made sharp, purchased a harp, and played several tunes with her chin.

conceptions.note: The register describes a technique and changes in expectations; this conception follows the particular verse rather than assigning an explicit theory to it.

left.reason: The verses show exaggerated and absurd situations but do not state that nonsense uses exaggeration; that relation is the register’s description of the technique.
